name: teamwork-task-analyze
description: Fetch a Teamwork.com task or whole tasklist by URL and prepare it for implementation. Pulls the task name, description, attachments, comments, comment-attached files, and subtasks via REST API v3 (reusing the shared config/token from the `teamwork-task` plugin), then deep-scans the current repository for related code/specs and interactively rewrites the task description into the canonical WAME format — additively, keeping everything the reporter already wrote verbatim at the top (inline screenshots and links included) and never writing the estimate into the description or the title: [optional preamble] → HR → Akceptačné kritériá → HR → Cieľ → HR → Technický popis (Claude Code Plan-Mode style — files, functions, DB schema, step-by-step). During analysis the skill pauses with AskUserQuestion for every clarifying question that arises and folds the answers back into the rewritten description. Reviews subtasks (updates outdated ones, proposes splitting tasks above 240 min into 2–6 atomic subtasks when AC suggest natural cut points; never forces a split for small tasks). The acceptance criteria also get the cross-cutting requirements that apply — menu entry and inbound links for a new screen, authorization for a new action, expected data volume for a new list — the same UI/UX, performance, security and reachability dimensions teamwork-task-test verifies at QA time. The technical plan also names the framework versions the repository actually has installed and the idiomatic feature to use for the task (plan only, never an acceptance criterion). Checks the time estimate using the WAME estimate methodology `wame-estimate-v2` — one number per task picked against fixed outcome anchors, no speedup factor and no risk buffer — sets one when missing, otherwise shows a highlighted warning with original vs proposed estimate and reasoning, never silently overwrites. Every Teamwork write (PATCH description, PUT estimate, POST subtask) is preceded by a preview and an explicit AskUserQuestion confirmation. For tasklist URLs reuses the `teamwork-task` filter — only tasks in a configured start column (default 'Ready for Development' or 'To Do') assigned to the current user are analysed for write-back; tasks off the board and the rest are listed read-only so the user can sanity-check teammates' work. Read-only against the board (never moves it) and against time logs (never writes one). Shares the API token config with `teamwork-task` and `teamwork-task-test` — set up once.
